request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 35.4% (95% band 21.9% to 57.9%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.6; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.42, 95% band [+2.04, +2.66]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 22.8% (95% band 13.7% to 26.3%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 159999: +0.3; >= 160000: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.14, 95% band [-1.86, -0.60]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 11.0% (95% band 1.7% to 12.7%); rank 3 to 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): falls by 0.50 (95% band [-0.74, -0.00]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 16,500 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 6.4% (95% band 0.9% to 12.3%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.24, 95% band [-0.57, +0.20]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 5.1% (95% band 0.5% to 9.6%); rank 3 to 8 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): rises by 0.56 (95% band [+0.02, +1.16]) from x = 0 (5th percentile) to x = 198,000 (95th percentile); the shape in between is not resolved at this sample size.
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 3.2% (95% band 0.0% to 6.7%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.11, 95% band [-0.07, +0.30]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.0% to 6.3%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.11, 95% band [-0.02, +0.61]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 5.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.03, 95% band [-0.00, +0.28]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.0% (95% band 0.0% to 5.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.00, 95% band [-0.58, +0.07]).

Interactions: the model has 19 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.8% (95% band 0.2% to 2.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.24 (95% band +1.89 to +2.51) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.60 (95% band +1.93 to +2.93) when `PAY_AMT1` = 16,500.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 16,500: -0.53 (95% band -0.79 to -0.01) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.18 (95% band -0.59 to +0.24) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.1%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.25 (95% band -1.87 to -0.61) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, -1.03 (95% band -2.22 to -0.54) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.37 (95% band -0.62 to +0.37) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.16 (95% band -0.57 to +0.33) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.54 (95% band +0.01 to +1.23) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +0.63 (95% band -0.08 to +1.10) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.34 (95% band -0.61 to +0.35) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.25 (95% band -0.63 to +0.15) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.4% (95% band 1.0% to 4.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.45 (95% band +1.81 to +2.72) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.36 (95% band +1.72 to +3.05) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.13 (95% band -1.85 to -0.59) when `PAY_0` = -2, -1.23 (95% band -2.02 to -0.48) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 1.3% (95% band 0.2% to 4.5%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.10 (95% band +1.59 to +2.57) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.52 (95% band +2.10 to +2.74) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.39 (95% band -0.02 to +1.08) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.80 (95% band +0.06 to +1.41) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.1% to 3.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.50 (95% band +2.07 to +2.74) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +2.03 (95% band +1.17 to +2.52) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,400.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,400: -0.21 (95% band -0.57 to +0.26) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.68 (95% band -1.44 to +0.04) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.12 (95% band -1.90 to -0.52) when `AGE` = 23, -1.16 (95% band -1.82 to -0.54) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.12 (95% band -0.11 to +0.29) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.08 (95% band -0.33 to +0.49) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 16,500: -0.56 (95% band -0.75 to +0.05) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.41 (95% band -0.72 to -0.00) when `BILL_AMT2` = 191,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 191,000: +0.08 (95% band -0.02 to +0.54) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.24 (95% band -0.04 to +0.80) when `PAY_AMT1` = 16,500.
- `LIMIT_BAL & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.12 (95% band -1.64 to -0.59) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, -0.93 (95% band -2.03 to -0.49) when `BILL_AMT1` = 198,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 198,000: +0.43 (95% band +0.01 to +1.53) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.61 (95% band +0.01 to +1.05) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.6%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 420,000: -1.20 (95% band -2.01 to -0.62) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.01 (95% band -1.85 to -0.51) when `PAY_AMT1` = 16,500.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 16,500: -0.62 (95% band -0.93 to -0.01) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.43 (95% band -0.69 to +0.02) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 420,000.
- `PAY_0 & EDUCATION`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.33 (95% band +1.99 to +2.66) when `EDUCATION` = 1, +2.45 (95% band +2.04 to +2.83) when `EDUCATION` = 3.
  Effect of `EDUCATION` from 1 to 3: +0.02 (95% band -0.00 to +0.27) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.13 (95% band +0.00 to +0.59) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- 8 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 2.0%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The most important driver of predicted default is the repayment status in the latest month, September 2005: applicants who were already one or more months behind (value 2 or higher) carry a much higher predicted risk, roughly +2 on the log-odds scale, compared with paying in full, while a one-month delay adds a smaller increase."},{"id":2,"text":"The size of the credit limit is the second most important driver: limits up to about 159,999 NT dollars push predicted risk up slightly, while limits of 160,000 NT dollars or more push it down, with a net change of about -1.1 between the 5th and 95th percentiles."},{"id":3,"text":"The amount paid in September 2005 has a moderate effect: going from no payment to about 16,500 NT dollars lowers predicted risk by about 0.5, though the uncertainty band reaches close to zero, so this effect is less certain than the first two."},{"id":4,"text":"The bill amount in September 2005 has a weaker effect: higher bills raise predicted risk by about 0.6 across the range, but the band is wide, so the size of this effect is only loosely pinned down."},{"id":5,"text":"The interactions matter mainly in how much the repayment status and the credit limit count: the penalty for being behind on payments is somewhat smaller for applicants with high payments in September, and the protective effect of a higher limit is somewhat weaker for applicants who are already behind, but most of these interaction effects are small and their bands overlap zero."},{"id":6,"text":"Age, education, and the payment amounts from July and August 2005 show no effect the data can distinguish from zero, so the data do not settle whether they affect predicted default at all."},{"id":7,"text":"Overall, the model's predictions are driven mainly by recent repayment behaviour and the credit limit, with bill and payment amounts playing a secondary and less certain role."}]}
